title.zh: 卷50 尉元 慕容白曜
title.raw: 卷50 尉元 慕容白曜 Volume 50: Wei Yuan, Murong Baiyao

sentences.zh: 尉元 慕容白曜

translations.literal: Wei Yuan; Murong Baiyao
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan and Murong Baiyao

sentences.zh: 尉元，字苟仁，代人也。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan, style name Gourou, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan, whose style name was Gourou, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 世為豪宗。

translations.literal: For generations his family were a powerful clan.
translations.idiomatic: His line for generations had been a great local house.

sentences.zh: 父目斤，勇略聞於當時。

translations.literal: His father Mujin was renowned in his day for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mujin was famed in his time for bravery and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 泰常中，為前將軍，從平虎牢，頗有軍功，拜中山太守。

translations.literal: During Taichang he served as Front General, followed in the pacification of Hulao, won considerable military merit, and was appointed Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era he became Front General, helped capture Hulao with substantial merit, and was named Administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 元年十九，以善射稱。

translations.literal: At age nineteen he was known for skill in archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nineteen he was already famed as a fine archer.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，為虎賁中郎將，轉羽林中郎，小心恭肅，以匪懈見知。

translations.literal: During Shenlu he served as Central Cadet of the Tiger guards, then transferred to Central Cadet of the Forest guards; careful and respectful, he was known for never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlu reign he was a tiger-guard cadet, then a forest-guard cadet, esteemed for steady, respectful service without slackening.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其寬雅有風貌，稍遷駕部給事中。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu admired his easy grace and bearing and gradually promoted him to Attendant of the Imperial Chariot Office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu valued his calm elegance and presence and steadily raised him to Attendant of the Imperial Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 從幸海隅，賜爵富城男，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor to the eastern coast, was enfeoffed as Baron of Fucheng, and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the imperial tour to the eastern coast he was enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng and named General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 和平中，遷北部尚書，加散騎常侍，進爵太昌侯，拜冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In Heping he was transferred to Director of the Northern Department, given the additional title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, advanced in rank to Marquis of Taichang, and appointed General Who Wins the Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: During Heping he rose to Director of the Northern Department with concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, was promoted to Marquis of Taichang, and named Champion General.

sentences.zh: 天安元年，薛安都以徐州內附，請師救援。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tian'an, Xue Andu submitted Xuzhou to the court and requested troops for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Tian'an 1 Xue Andu brought Xuzhou over to Wei and asked for military aid.

sentences.zh: 顯祖以元為使持節、都督東道諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、博陵公，與城陽公孔伯恭赴之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen appointed Yuan as credential-bearing commissioner, Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Route armies, General Who Guards the South, Duke of Boling, and sent him with Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen made Yuan envoy with full credentials, supreme commander on the eastern front, General Who Guards the South, and Duke of Boling, and dispatched him with Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong.

sentences.zh: 劉彧東平太守、無鹽戍主申纂詐降。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's Administrator of Dongping and garrison commander of Wuyan, Shen Zuan, feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuan, Liu Yu's Dongping prefect and commander at Wuyan, pretended to submit.

sentences.zh: 元知非誠款，外示容納，而密備焉。

translations.literal: Yuan knew the offer was not sincere; outwardly he showed acceptance while secretly making preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan saw the surrender was false, welcomed it in appearance, and quietly prepared his defenses.

sentences.zh: 劉彧兗州刺史畢眾敬遣東平太守章仇𢷋詣軍歸款，元並納之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Yanzhou Bi Zhongjing sent the Administrator of Dongping Zhang Chou to the army to submit; Yuan accepted him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing, Liu Yu's Yanzhou inspector, sent Dongping prefect Zhang Chou to surrender; Yuan took him in too.

sentences.zh: 遂長驅而進，賊將周凱望聲遁走。

translations.literal: He then drove forward at length; the enemy general Zhou Kai fled at the sound of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on in force, and the rebel commander Zhou Kai fled before his advance.

sentences.zh: 彧遣將張永、沈攸之等率眾討安都，屯于下磕。

translations.literal: Yu dispatched the generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi and others with troops to attack Andu, encamping at Xiake.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, and others against Andu and camped at Xiake.

sentences.zh: 永乃分遣羽林監王穆之領卒五千，守輜重於武原，龍驤將軍謝善居領卒二千據呂梁，散騎侍郎張引領卒二千守茱萸，督上租糧，供其軍實。

translations.literal: Yong then detached the Forest guard supervisor Wang Muzhi with five thousand men to guard the baggage at Wuyuan, the Dragon-cavalry General Xie Shanjü with two thousand to hold Liang, and the Cavalier Attendant Zhang Yin with two thousand to guard Zhuyu, supervising the delivery of tax grain to supply his army.
translations.idiomatic: Yong posted Wang Muzhi with five thousand men to guard supplies at Wuyuan, Xie Shanjü with two thousand at Liang, and Zhang Yin with two thousand at Zhuyu to collect grain taxes for the army.

sentences.zh: 安都出城見元，元依朝旨，授其徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Andu came out of the city to see Yuan; Yuan, following the court's order, appointed him Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Andu came out to meet Yuan, who by imperial instruction confirmed him as Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣中書侍郎高閭、李璨等與安都俱還入城，別令孔伯恭精甲二千，撫安內外，然後元入彭城。

translations.literal: He sent the Secretariat Attendant Gao Lü, Li Can, and others back into the city with Andu, while separately ordering Kong Bogong with two thousand picked troops to pacify the interior and exterior; only then did Yuan enter Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Secretariat attendants Gao Lü and Li Can into the city with Andu, left Kong Bogong with two thousand elite troops to steady the garrison, and then entered Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 元以張永仍據險要，攻守勢倍，懼傷士卒。

translations.literal: Yuan, because Zhang Yong still held strong positions and the balance of attack and defense was doubled against him, feared injury to his troops.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Yong still holding key ground and the odds of attack and defense against him, Yuan feared heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 乃命安都與璨等固守，身率精銳，揚兵於外，分擊呂梁，絕其糧運。

translations.literal: He then ordered Andu and Can and the rest to hold firm while he personally led picked troops to display force outside, striking Liang in separate columns and cutting off their grain supply.
translations.idiomatic: He had Andu and Can hold the line while he led crack troops abroad, raiding Liang and severing their grain route.

sentences.zh: 善居遁奔茱萸，仍與張引東走武原。

translations.literal: Shanjü fled to Zhuyu, then with Zhang Yin went east toward Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjü abandoned Liang for Zhuyu, then fled east with Zhang Yin toward Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 馳騎追擊，斬首八百餘級。

translations.literal: Cavalry were sent in pursuit; more than eight hundred heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing cavalry cut down more than eight hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 武原窮寇八千餘人，拒戰不下。

translations.literal: At Wuyuan more than eight thousand cornered enemy troops resisted and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Eight thousand trapped enemy soldiers at Wuyuan still refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 元親擐甲胄，四面攻之，破穆之外營，殺傷太半，獲其輜重五百餘乘，以給彭城諸軍。

translations.literal: Yuan personally donned armor and attacked on four sides, broke Muzhi's outer camp, killed or wounded more than half, and captured more than five hundred supply carts to furnish the Pengcheng armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan himself armored and assaulted from four sides, overran Muzhi's outer camp, killed or wounded more than half, and seized over five hundred supply wagons for the Pengcheng force.

sentences.zh: 然後收師緩戰，開其走路。

translations.literal: He then drew off his troops and fought more slowly, opening a path for their escape.
translations.idiomatic: He then eased the assault and opened a way out for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 穆之率餘燼奔于永軍。

translations.literal: Muzhi led the remnant flames to Yong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi rallied the survivors and joined Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 永勢挫力屈，元乘勝圍之，攻其南門，永遂捐城夜遁。

translations.literal: Yong's strength was broken and his force spent; Yuan took advantage to besiege him, attacked the south gate, and Yong abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong's power collapsed Yuan pressed the siege, stormed the south gate, and Yong fled the city at night.

sentences.zh: 伯恭、安都乘勢追擊，時大雨雪，泗水冰合，永棄船而走。

translations.literal: Bogong and Andu pursued by force; at the time heavy rain and snow fell, the Si River froze solid, and Yong abandoned his boats and fled on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong and Andu pursued hard; in driving snow the Si froze, and Yong left his boats and ran.

sentences.zh: 元豫測永必將奔亡，身率眾軍，邀其走路，南北奮擊，大破於呂梁之東。

translations.literal: Yuan foresaw that Yong would certainly flee, personally led the army to block his route, and struck fiercely north and south, routing him east of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting Yong to run, Yuan himself blocked the escape route and smashed the enemy east of Liang.

sentences.zh: 斬首數萬級，追北六十餘里，死者相枕，手足凍斷者十八九。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of heads were cut; the pursuit ran more than sixty li; the dead lay pillow to pillow, and eight or nine in ten had frozen hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: The slaughter numbered in the tens of thousands; the chase went sixty-odd li; corpses lay heaped, and eight or nine of ten survivors had frozen limbs.

sentences.zh: 生擒劉彧使持節，都督梁、南、北秦三州諸軍事，梁、秦二州刺史，寧朔將軍，益陽縣開國侯垣恭祖；

translations.literal: Captured alive were Liu Yu's credential-bearing commissioner, Commander-in-Chief of Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, Inspector of Liang and Qin, General Who Pacifies the North, Marquis of Yiyang, Yuan Gongzu;
translations.idiomatic: They took alive Liu Yu's envoy Yuan Gongzu, commander of Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, inspector of Liang and Qin, General Who Pacifies the North, and Marquis of Yiyang;

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍、羽林監沈承伯等。

translations.literal: the Dragon-cavalry General and Forest guard supervisor Shen Chengbo and others.
translations.idiomatic: along with Dragon-cavalry General and Forest guard supervisor Shen Chengbo and others.

sentences.zh: 永、攸之輕騎走免。

translations.literal: Yong and Youzhi escaped on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi got away on swift mounts.

sentences.zh: 收其船車軍資器械不可勝數。

translations.literal: Boats, carts, military stores, and weapons captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The boats, wagons, stores, and arms taken were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 劉彧東徐州刺史張讜據團城，徐州刺史王玄載守下邳，輔國將軍、兗州刺史樊昌侯王整，龍驤將軍、蘭陵太守桓忻驅掠近民，保險自固。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou Zhang Dan held Tuan city, Inspector of Xuzhou Wang Xuanzai held Xiapi, the Assistant General and Inspector of Yanzhou Marquis of Fanchang Wang Zheng, and the Dragon-cavalry General and Administrator of Lanling Huan Xin drove off nearby people and held strong places to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dan held Tuan as Liu Yu's Eastern Xuzhou inspector, Wang Xuanzai held Xiapi, Wang Zheng and Huan Xin raided the countryside and fortified themselves.

sentences.zh: 元遣慰喻，張讜及青州刺史沈文秀等皆遣使通誠，王整、桓忻相與歸命。

translations.literal: Yuan sent envoys to reassure them; Zhang Dan and the Inspector of Qingzhou Shen Wenxiu and others all sent envoys pledging loyalty, and Wang Zheng and Huan Xin together submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent reassuring messages; Zhang Dan, Qingzhou inspector Shen Wenxiu, and others sent pledges of loyalty, and Wang Zheng and Huan Xin submitted together.

sentences.zh: 元表曰：「彭城倉廩虛罄，人有飢色，求運冀、相、濟、兗四州粟，取張永所棄船九百艘，沿清運致，可以濟救新民。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized: "The Pengcheng granaries are empty and the people show hunger; I request grain from Ji, Xiang, Ji, and Yanzhou, using the nine hundred boats Zhang Yong abandoned to ship it along the Qing River—this can relieve the new subjects."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan reported that Pengcheng's stores were bare and the people hungry, and asked grain from four provinces shipped on Zhang Yong's nine hundred abandoned boats along the Qing to feed the new subjects.

sentences.zh: 」顯祖從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen agreed.

sentences.zh: 又表分兵置戍，進定青冀。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to detach troops for garrisons and advance to secure Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to post garrisons and press on to settle Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 復表曰：「彭城賊之要蕃，不有積粟強守，不可以固。

translations.literal: He memorialized again: "Pengcheng is the enemy's vital barrier; without stored grain and a strong defense it cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote that Pengcheng was the enemy's key fortress and could not be held without grain and a stout garrison.

sentences.zh: 若儲糧廣戍，雖劉彧師徒悉動，不敢窺𨵦淮北之地。

translations.literal: If grain is stored and garrisons broadened, even if Liu Yu moves his whole army he will not dare look toward the north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: With ample stores and widespread posts, even a full Liu Yu offensive would not dare cross north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 此自然之勢也。

translations.literal: This is the natural tendency of things."
translations.idiomatic: That, he said, was the natural course of events.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「待後軍到，量宜守防。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When the rear army arrives, gauge what is fit for defense."
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied that when the rear army arrived he should judge how best to defend.

sentences.zh: 其青冀已遣軍援，須待克定，更運軍糧。

translations.literal: Troops have already been sent to aid Qing and Ji; wait until they are secured, then transport army grain again."
translations.idiomatic: Aid was already on the way to Qing and Ji; more grain would follow once those regions were taken.

sentences.zh: 」元又表曰：「臣受命出疆，再離寒暑，[1]進無鄧艾一舉之功，退無羊祜保境之略，雖淮岱獲振，而民情未安。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized again: "Your servant received orders beyond the borders and has twice passed through cold and heat; in advance there is not the achievement of Deng Ai's single stroke, in retreat not the strategy of Yang Hu's guarding the frontier—though the Huai and Dai are stirred, the people's hearts are not yet at peace."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wrote again that he had campaigned two seasons without Deng Ai's decisive victory or Yang Hu's steady frontier policy, and though the Huai region trembled the people were still uneasy.

sentences.zh: 臣以愚智，屬當偏任，苟事宜宣徹，敢不以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant, with foolish wisdom, has been placed in a partial command; if affairs should be carried through I dare not fail to report."
translations.idiomatic: He said that holding a limited command he would report whatever must be done.

sentences.zh: 臣前表以下邳水陸所湊，先規殄滅，遣兵屢討，猶未擒定。

translations.literal: In my former memorial I noted that Xiapi is a gathering place by water and land; I first planned to destroy it and have repeatedly sent troops, yet it is still not taken."
translations.idiomatic: He recalled his earlier plan to crush Xiapi, the junction of land and water routes, though repeated attacks had not taken it.

sentences.zh: 然彭城、下邳信命未斷，而此城之人，元居賊界，心尚戀土。

translations.literal: Yet Pengcheng and Xiapi have not broken faith, while the people of this city, Yuan being in enemy territory, still cling to their land.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng and Xiapi still held out, and people in enemy-held towns still yearned for home.

sentences.zh: 輒相誑惑，希幸非望，南來息耗，壅塞不達，雖至窮迫，仍不肯降。

translations.literal: They deceive one another, hoping for the unlikely; news from the south is blocked and does not arrive, and though driven to extremity they still will not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They deluded one another with false hopes, southern news was cut off, and even in desperation they refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 彭城民任玄朗從淮南到鎮，稱劉彧將任農夫、陳顯達領兵三千，來循宿豫。

translations.literal: A Pengcheng man, Ren Xuanlang, coming from Huainan to the garrison, said Liu Yu's generals Ren Nongfu and Chen Xianda were leading three thousand men toward Suqian.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xuanlang of Pengcheng, arriving from Huainan, said Liu Yu's Ren Nongfu and Chen Xianda were marching three thousand men on Suqian.

sentences.zh: 臣即以其日，密遣覘使，驗其虛實，如朗所言。

translations.literal: That very day your servant secretly sent scouts to verify the report, and it matched what Lang said.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent scouts the same day and found Lang's report true.

sentences.zh: 臣欲自出擊之，以運糧未接，又恐新民生變，遣子都將于沓千、劉龍駒等步騎五千，將往赴擊。

translations.literal: Your servant wished to strike in person, but because grain had not yet arrived and fearing unrest among the new subjects, he sent the subordinate generals Yu Taqian and Liu Longju with five thousand infantry and cavalry to go and attack.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to lead the attack himself but, with supplies still short and fearing unrest among new subjects, sent Yu Taqian and Liu Longju with five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 但征人淹久，逃亡者多，迭相扇動，莫有固志，器仗敗毀，無一可用。

translations.literal: But the campaign troops had been long abroad; many had fled, stirring one another so that none held firm will, and weapons were ruined so that not one was usable.
translations.idiomatic: The army had been in the field too long; deserters stirred one another, morale collapsed, and arms were ruined beyond use.

sentences.zh: 臣聞伐國事重，古人所難，功雖可立，必須經略而舉。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that attacking a state is weighty and difficult for the ancients; though merit may be established, it must be undertaken with planning.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that conquering a state was grave work even for antiquity and required careful planning.

sentences.zh: 若賊向彭城，必由清泗過宿豫，歷下邳；

translations.literal: If the enemy moves on Pengcheng they must pass Suqian along the Qing and Si, then Xiapi;
translations.idiomatic: An enemy thrust at Pengcheng would come by Suqian on the Qing and Si, then Xiapi;

sentences.zh: 趨青州，路亦由下邳入沂水，經東安。

translations.literal: heading for Qingzhou, the route also enters the Yi from Xiapi, passing Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: and toward Qingzhou would likewise pass Xiapi into the Yi and through Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 即為賊用師之要。

translations.literal: These are the essentials of the enemy's use of troops."
translations.idiomatic: Those were the enemy's critical lines of march.

sentences.zh: 今若先定下邳，平宿豫，鎮淮陽，戍東安，則青冀諸鎮可不攻而克。

translations.literal: If we first take Xiapi, pacify Suqian, garrison Huaiyang, and guard Dong'an, then the garrisons of Qing and Ji can be taken without attack.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiapi, Suqian, Huaiyang, and Dong'an were secured first, Qing and Ji would fall without a fight.

sentences.zh: 若四處不服，青冀雖拔，百姓狼顧，猶懷僥倖之心。

translations.literal: If the four places do not submit, though Qing and Ji are seized the people will look back in alarm and still harbor hope.
translations.idiomatic: If those posts held out, even a Qing-Ji victory would leave the people restless and hopeful.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜釋青冀之師，先定東南之地，斷劉彧北顧之意，絕愚民南望之心。

translations.literal: Your servant in his folly thinks we should release the Qing-Ji army, first settle the southeast, cut Liu Yu's glance northward, and end the foolish people's longing to look south.
translations.idiomatic: He urged abandoning the Qing-Ji offensive to secure the southeast first, blocking Liu Yu's northern ambitions and southern illusions.

sentences.zh: 夏水雖盛，無津途可因；

translations.literal: Though summer waters are high, there is no ford to use;
translations.idiomatic: Summer floods offered no ford;

sentences.zh: 冬路雖通，無高城可固。

translations.literal: though winter roads are open, there is no high wall to hold."
translations.idiomatic: winter routes were open but no strong walls could be held.

sentences.zh: 如此，則淮北自舉，暫勞永逸。

translations.literal: Thus north of the Huai would rise of itself—a brief toil for lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: Then the north Huai would submit of itself at the cost of one sharp effort.

sentences.zh: 今雖向熱，猶可行師，兵尚神速，久則生變。

translations.literal: Though it is now hot, troops may still march; in war speed is prized, and delay breeds change.
translations.idiomatic: Even in heat an army could move; speed mattered, for delay bred trouble.

sentences.zh: 若天雨既降，或因水通，運糧益眾，規為進取。

translations.literal: If rain falls and water opens the routes, grain transport will grow and plans for advance may be made.
translations.idiomatic: Rain might open the waterways, swell convoys, and invite a new offensive.

sentences.zh: 恐近淮民庶，翻然改圖，青冀二州，卒未可拔。

translations.literal: I fear the people near the Huai will suddenly change heart, and Qing and Ji in the end cannot be seized."
translations.idiomatic: He feared Huai border folk would turn, leaving Qing and Ji untaken.

sentences.zh: 臣輒與僚佐共議，咸謂可然。

translations.literal: Your servant has discussed with his staff, and all say it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: His staff agreed the plan was sound.

sentences.zh: 若隱而不陳，懼有損敗之責；

translations.literal: If I conceal and do not report, I fear the blame of loss and defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Silence would risk blame for defeat;

sentences.zh: 陳而無驗，恐成誣罔之罪。

translations.literal: if I report and it is not verified, I fear the crime of falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: speaking without result would risk the charge of deception.

sentences.zh: 惟天鑒懸量，照臣愚款。」

translations.literal: May Heaven's mirror hang high and illuminate your servant's sincere intent."
translations.idiomatic: He asked Heaven to judge his honest intent.

sentences.zh: 彧復遣沈攸之、吳憘公領卒數萬，從沂清而進，欲援下邳。

translations.literal: Yu again sent Shen Youzhi and Duke of Wu Xi with tens of thousands of men advancing along the Yi and Qing to relieve Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Shen Youzhi and Duke of Wu Xi with tens of thousands along the Yi and Qing to save Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 元遣孔伯恭率步騎一萬以拒之。

translations.literal: Yuan sent Kong Bogong with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent Kong Bogong with ten thousand foot and horse to block them.

sentences.zh: 并以攸之前敗軍人傷殘手足、瘃 膝行者，[2]盡送令還，以沮其眾。

translations.literal: He also sent back all the wounded soldiers from Youzhi's earlier defeat whose hands and feet were injured and whose knees were frostbitten, to discourage their host.
translations.idiomatic: He returned every maimed survivor of Youzhi's earlier rout—men with ruined hands and feet and frostbitten knees—to break enemy morale.

sentences.zh: 又表求濟師。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked the throne for more troops.

sentences.zh: 詔遣征南大將軍慕容白曜赴之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched the Campaigning South General Murong Baiyao to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Campaigning South General Murong Baiyao to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 白曜到瑕丘，遇患。

translations.literal: Baiyao reached Xiqiu and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao reached Xiqiu but took sick.

sentences.zh: 會泗水暴竭，賊軍不得前進，白曜遂不行。

translations.literal: Just then the Si River suddenly dried, so the enemy army could not advance, and Baiyao therefore did not march.
translations.idiomatic: The Si abruptly ran dry, the enemy could not advance, and Baiyao halted.

sentences.zh: 伯恭大破賊軍，攸之、憘公等輕騎遁走。

translations.literal: Bogong routed the enemy army; Youzhi, Duke of Wu, and the rest fled on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong shattered the enemy; Youzhi and Duke of Wu escaped on swift horses.

sentences.zh: 元書與劉彧徐州刺史王玄載，示其禍福。

translations.literal: Yuan wrote to Liu Yu's Inspector of Xuzhou Wang Xuanzai, showing him fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wrote Wang Xuanzai, Liu Yu's Xuzhou inspector, spelling out the consequences.

sentences.zh: 玄載狼狽夜走，宿豫、淮陽皆棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Xuanzai fled in panic by night; Suqian and Huaiyang both abandoned their cities and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzai bolted by night; Suqian and Huaiyang were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 於是遣南中郎將、中書侍郎高閭領騎一千，與張讜對為東徐州刺史；

translations.literal: He then sent the Southern Gentlemen General and Secretariat Attendant Gao Lü with a thousand horse to pair with Zhang Dan as Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He posted Secretariat attendant Gao Lü with a thousand cavalry to serve with Zhang Dan as Eastern Xuzhou inspector;

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎李璨與畢眾敬對為東兗州刺史。

translations.literal: the Secretariat Attendant Li Can to pair with Bi Zhongjing as Inspector of Eastern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Can with Bi Zhongjing as Eastern Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 以安初附。

translations.literal: This was to settle those who had just submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments were meant to steady the newly submitted regions.

sentences.zh: 拜元都督徐、南、北兗州諸軍事，鎮東大將軍，開府，徐州刺史，淮陽公，持節、散騎常侍、尚書如故。

translations.literal: Yuan was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Xu, Southern Yan, and Northern Yanzhou, General Who Guards the East, with an office opened, Inspector of Xuzhou, Duke of Huaiyang, retaining his credential-bearing status, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Director posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was made commander of Xu and the Yan provinces, General Who Guards the East, with an opened staff, Xuzhou inspector, Duke of Huaiyang, keeping his credentials and court posts.

sentences.zh: 詔元曰：「賊將沈攸之、吳憘公等驅率蟻眾，進寇下邳，卿戎昭果毅，智勇奮發，水陸邀絕，應時摧殄，自淮以北，蕩然清定。

translations.literal: An edict to Yuan said: "The enemy generals Shen Youzhi and Duke of Wu Xi and others drive ant-like masses to invade Xiapi; you, martial and resolute, wise and brave, cut them off by land and water and destroyed them in season, so that north of the Huai is suddenly clear."
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised Yuan for crushing Shen Youzhi and Duke of Wu Xi's swarm at Xiapi by land and water, clearing the north Huai.

sentences.zh: 皆是元帥經略，將士效力之所致也，朕用嘉焉。

translations.literal: All this is due to the commander-in-chief's planning and the officers' exertion; We are pleased."
translations.idiomatic: The victory, the edict said, came from the commander's strategy and the troops' effort, and the emperor rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 所獲諸城要害之處，分兵置戍，以帖民情。

translations.literal: At every captured strong place detach troops for garrisons to steady the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered garrisons at every captured strongpoint to calm the people.

sentences.zh: 今方欲清蕩吳會，懸旌秣陵，至於用兵所宜，形勢進止，善加量度，動靜以聞。」

translations.literal: Now We intend to sweep Wu and Yue and plant banners at Moling; as to what troops should do, how forces should move or halt—measure well and report your movements."
translations.idiomatic: The court would next sweep the southeast toward Moling; Yuan should weigh every move and report.

sentences.zh: 是時徐州妖人假姓司馬，字休符，自稱晉王，扇惑百姓。

translations.literal: At that time a sorcerer in Xuzhou took the false surname Sima, style name Xiufu, called himself King of Jin, and incited the people.
translations.idiomatic: A Xuzhou mystic falsely surnamed himself Sima Xiufu, proclaimed himself King of Jin, and stirred the populace.

sentences.zh: 元遣將追斬之。

translations.literal: Yuan sent generals to pursue and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent troops who ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔徵元還京赴西郊，尋還所鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict summoned Yuan to the capital for the western suburb rites; he soon returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Yuan was recalled to the capital for the western suburb ceremony, then returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 延興元年五月，假元淮陽王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yanxing, Yuan was given the nominal title Prince of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing 1, fifth month, Yuan was made Prince of Huaiyang in name.

sentences.zh: 三年，劉昱將蕭順之、王勑懃等領眾三萬，入寇淮北諸城，元分遣諸將，逆擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third year Liu Yu's generals Xiao Shunzhi, Wang Qin, and others led thirty thousand men to invade the Huai-north cities; Yuan detached generals to meet and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Xiao Shunzhi and Wang Qin led thirty thousand against the Huai-north towns; Yuan's generals repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 元表：「淮陽郡上黨令韓念祖始臨之初，舊民南叛，全無一人。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized: "When Han Nianzu first took office as magistrate of Shangdang in Huaiyang commandery, the old subjects had all fled south and not one remained."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan reported that when Han Nianzu became magistrate of Shangdang in Huaiyang the old population had all fled south.

sentences.zh: 令撫綏招集，愛民如子，南來民費係先等前後歸附，戶至二百有餘。

translations.literal: The magistrate comforted and gathered them, loving the people as his children; southerners such as Fei Xixian and others successively returned, and households reached more than two hundred."
translations.idiomatic: Nianzu gathered them with parental care until more than two hundred households, including Fei Xixian from the south, had returned.

sentences.zh: 南濟陰郡睢陵縣人趙憐等辭稱念祖善於綏撫，清身潔己，請乞念祖為睢陵令。

translations.literal: Zhao Lian and others of Suiling county in Southern Jiyin commandery petitioned that Nianzu was skilled at soothing the people and kept himself pure, and asked that Nianzu be made magistrate of Suiling.
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners from Suiling in Southern Jiyin asked that Nianzu, praised for gentle rule and personal integrity, be transferred to Suiling.

sentences.zh: 若得其人，必能招集離叛，成立一縣。

translations.literal: If such a man is obtained, he will surely be able to gather those who have fled and establish a whole county."
translations.idiomatic: With such a man, they said, he could rally the displaced and build a full county.

sentences.zh: 」顯祖詔曰：「樹君為民，民情如此，可聽如請。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen decreed: "To plant rulers for the people—when the people's feeling is thus, grant the request."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen replied that when the people asked so plainly, the appointment should be granted.

sentences.zh: 」元好申下人之善，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Yuan was fond of commending the merits of subordinates—this was all of a piece.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan liked to bring forward the virtues of his subordinates; cases like this were typical.

sentences.zh: 太和初，徵為內都大官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was summoned as Grand Director of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he was recalled to serve as Grand Director of the Inner Capital.

sentences.zh: 既而出為使持節、鎮西大將車、開府、統萬鎮都將，甚得夷民之心。

translations.literal: He then went out as credential-bearing commissioner, General Who Guards the West, with an office opened, and Commander-in-Chief of the Tongwan Garrison, and won the hearts of the frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out with full credentials as General Who Guards the West, with an opened staff and command at Tongwan, and deeply won the trust of the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 三年，進爵淮陽王，以舊老見禮，聽乘步挽，杖於朝。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to Prince of Huaiyang; as an elder of former service he was shown honor, permitted to ride in a hand-drawn carriage, and lean on a staff at court.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was raised to Prince of Huaiyang, honored as an elder, allowed a hand-drawn carriage, and a court staff at audience.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成既自立，多遣間諜，扇動新民，不逞之徒，所在蜂起。

translations.literal: After Xiao Daocheng had established himself, he sent many spies to stir the new subjects, and unruly men rose everywhere like bees.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiao Daocheng seized power he sent agents to agitate the newly submitted population, and malcontents swarmed up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 以元威名夙振，徵為使持節、侍中、都督南征諸軍事、征西大將軍、大都將，餘官如故，總率諸軍以討之。

translations.literal: Because Yuan's prestige had long been formidable, he was summoned as credential-bearing commissioner, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Campaign armies, General Who Campaigns West, Grand Commander, with other posts as before, to lead all armies in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: His renown led the court to recall him as envoy and Palace Attendant, supreme commander of the southern campaign, General Who Campaigns West, and Grand Commander, with all prior titles, to crush the unrest.

sentences.zh: 元討五固賊桓和等，皆平之。

translations.literal: Yuan attacked the Wugu bandits Huan He and others and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan attacked the Wugu rebels under Huan He and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 東南清晏，遠近帖然。

translations.literal: The southeast was cleared and calm; far and near were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast grew quiet and distant regions submitted.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、都曹尚書，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant and Director of the Capital Bureau, then was transferred to Director of the Masters.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Capital Bureau, then became Director of the Masters.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進位司徒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen he rose to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 十六年，例降庶姓王爵，封山陽郡開國公，食邑六百戶。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, by precedent the noble surname princedoms were reduced; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shanyang commandery with an open state, fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen, when princely surnames were reduced by statute, he became Duke of Shanyang with six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 元表曰：「臣以天安之初，奉律總戎，廓寧淮右，海內既平，仍忝徐岳。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized: "Your servant, from the beginning of Tian'an, received orders to command troops, pacified the right bank of the Huai, and when the realm was settled still held Xu and the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wrote that since Tian'an he had commanded armies, pacified the Huai right bank, and even after peace still held the Xu region.

sentences.zh: [3]素餐尸祿，積有年歲，彼土安危，竊所具悉。

translations.literal: [3] Eating salary without merit, accumulating years; the safety of that land your servant knows in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He had drawn salary for years without fresh merit yet knew that region's dangers intimately.

sentences.zh: 每惟彭城水陸之要，江南用兵，莫不因之威陵諸夏。

translations.literal: I constantly reflect that Pengcheng is the strategic junction of water and land; whenever the south uses troops, they must rely on it to overawe the central states.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng's waterways made it the hinge of every southern campaign against the heartland.

sentences.zh: 夫國之大計，豫備為先。

translations.literal: A state's great plan puts preparation first.
translations.idiomatic: For any state, foresight must come first.

sentences.zh: 且臣初克徐方，青齊未定，從河以南，猶懷彼此。

translations.literal: Moreover when your servant first took Xuzhou, Qing and Ji were not yet settled, and south of the Yellow River minds still wavered between the two sides.
translations.idiomatic: When he first secured Xuzhou, Qing and Ji were unsettled and hearts south of the Yellow River still wavered.

sentences.zh: 時劉彧遣張永、沈攸之、陳顯達、蕭順之等前後數度，規取彭城，勢連青兗。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu sent Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, Chen Xianda, Xiao Shunzhi, and others several times to plan taking Pengcheng, their momentum linking Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had repeatedly sent Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, Chen Xianda, Xiao Shunzhi, and others against Pengcheng, linking Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 唯以彭城既固，而永等摧屈。

translations.literal: Only because Pengcheng was firm did Yong and the rest be broken and bent.
translations.idiomatic: Only Pengcheng's strength had broken those attempts.

sentences.zh: 今計彼戍兵，多是胡人，臣前鎮徐州之日，胡人子都將呼延籠達因於負罪，便爾叛亂，鳩引胡類，一時扇動。

translations.literal: Now I calculate that their garrison troops are mostly barbarians; when your servant formerly held Xuzhou, the barbarian subordinate general Huyan Longda, because of a crime, at once rebelled, gathering barbarians and stirring them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that enemy garrisons were mostly non-Chinese; Huyan Longda had once rebelled from Xuzhou and roused the tribes.

sentences.zh: 賴威靈遐被，罪人斯戮。

translations.literal: Relying on awesome might reaching far, the guilty man was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial might had reached him and the rebel was executed.

sentences.zh: 又團城子都將胡人王敕懃負釁南叛，每懼姦圖，狡誘同黨。

translations.literal: Also the Tuan city subordinate general, the barbarian Wang Qin, bore guilt and fled south, and I constantly feared treacherous plots and crafty enticement of his fellows.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qin of Tuan, another tribal officer, had fled south after a crime, and Yuan still feared his intrigues.

sentences.zh: 愚誠所見，[4]宜以彭城胡軍換取南豫州徙民之兵，轉戍彭城；

translations.literal: What your servant's foolish sincerity sees [4] is that the Pengcheng barbarian army should be exchanged for troops of relocated people from Southern Yuzhou, transferred to garrison Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed swapping Pengcheng's tribal garrison for relocated troops from Southern Yuzhou and posting them at Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 又以中州鮮卑增實兵數。

translations.literal: and also increasing the Central Province Xianbei to fill out the army numbers.
translations.idiomatic: and reinforcing the ranks with Central Province Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 於事為宜。

translations.literal: For affairs this is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: That, he argued, was the sound course.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「公之所陳，甚合事機。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "What the Duke has stated fits the situation very well."
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied that his plan matched the needs of the moment.

sentences.zh: 其年，頻表以老乞身。

translations.literal: That year he repeatedly memorialized, citing age to beg leave of office.
translations.idiomatic: That year he repeatedly asked to retire on account of age.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔曰：「元年尊識遠，屢表告退。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict said: "From the first year your honored insight has been far-reaching and you have repeatedly memorialized to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor noted that Yuan had sought retirement since the first year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 朕以公秉德清挹，體懷平隱，仁雅淵廣，謀猷是仗，方委之民政，用康億兆，故頻文累札，仍違沖志。

translations.literal: We, because the Duke holds pure virtue, a bearing of calm restraint, humane elegance broad and deep, and counsel on which We rely, were about to entrust civil affairs to bring peace to the millions—thus repeated documents still went against your lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Yuan's virtue and counsel and had wished to keep him in civil service, yet Yuan's repeated requests refused that intent.

sentences.zh: 而謙光逾固，三請彌切，若不屈從高謨，復何以成其美德也。

translations.literal: Yet your modesty grew firmer and three requests more urgent; if We did not yield to your high counsel, how could We complete your beautiful virtue?
translations.idiomatic: His modesty only deepened; to honor his virtue the throne must grant retirement.

sentences.zh: 已許其致仕，主者可出表付外，如禮申遂。

translations.literal: We have approved your retirement; the chief official should issue the memorial abroad and carry it through according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Retirement was granted and the ministries were to proceed by ritual.

sentences.zh: 」元詣闕謝老，引見於庭，命昇殿勞宴，賜玄冠素服。

translations.literal: Yuan came to the palace to thank for old age, was received in audience in the hall, ordered to ascend the steps for a feast of consolation, and was given a dark cap and plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan came to court to thank the emperor, was received in the hall, feasted, and given ceremonial cap and plain robes.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「夫大道凝虛，至德沖挹，故后王法玄猷以御世，[5]聖人崇謙光而降美。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The Great Way congeals in emptiness; supreme virtue is poured out in restraint—thus later kings use the dark teaching to govern the age, [5] and sages honor modest light and lower their beauty.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict praised the Way's emptiness and the sage's humility as models for kings.

sentences.zh: 是以天子父事三老，兄事五更，所以明孝悌於萬國，垂教本于天下。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven treats the Three Elders as a father and the Five Worthies as elder brothers, to make filial piety clear to the ten thousand states and extend the root of teaching throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Son of Heaven fathered the Three Elders and elder-brothered the Five Worthies to spread filial teaching under heaven.

sentences.zh: 自非道高識博，孰能處之？

translations.literal: Unless the Way is high and knowledge broad, who can occupy such a place?
translations.idiomatic: Only men of vast learning could fill such roles.

sentences.zh: 是故五帝憲德，三王乞言，若求備一人，同之古哲，叔世之老，孰能克堪？

translations.literal: Thus the Five Emperors honored virtue, the Three Kings begged for words; if one sought a complete man equal to the sages of old, who in a degenerate age's elder could measure up?
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors revered worthies and the Three Kings sought counsel, yet few elders of a fallen age could match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 師上聖則難為其舉，傅中庸則易為其選。

translations.literal: To take a supreme sage as teacher is hard to accomplish; to take a middling worthy is easy to choose.
translations.idiomatic: A teacher of supreme sainthood was hard to find; a middling worthy was easier to appoint.

sentences.zh: 朕既虛寡，德謝曩哲，更、老之選，差可有之。

translations.literal: We, though empty and few in virtue, falling short of past sages, a choice of Worthies and Elders may yet be possible.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confessed his modest virtue yet thought elders might still be chosen.

sentences.zh: 前司徒、山陽郡開國公尉元，前大鴻臚卿、新泰伯游明根並元亨利貞，明允誠素，少著英風，老敷雅迹，位顯台宿，歸終私第。

translations.literal: The former Minister of Education, Duke of Shanyang commandery Wei Yuan, and the former Grand Herald, Marquis of Xintai You Minggen—both yuan, heng, li, and zhen, bright and sincere—showed heroic wind in youth and spread elegant traces in age; their stations shone in the constellations of office, their ends came in private homes.
translations.idiomatic: Former Minister Wei Yuan and former Grand Herald You Minggen were named as paragons of constancy from youth to age.

sentences.zh: 可謂知始知卒，希世之賢也。

translations.literal: They may be called knowing beginning and end—sages rare in the age.
translations.idiomatic: They knew their beginning and end, rare worthies of the time.

sentences.zh: 公以八十之年，宜處三老之重；

translations.literal: The Duke, at eighty years, should occupy the weight of the Three Elders;
translations.idiomatic: At eighty, Yuan should stand as one of the Three Elders;

sentences.zh: 卿以七十之齡，可充五更之選。

translations.literal: the Minister, at seventy years, may fill the choice of the Five Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: at seventy, Minggen might serve among the Five Worthies.

sentences.zh: 」於是養三老五更於明堂，國老庶老於階下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Three Elders and Five Worthies were nurtured in the Bright Hall, the state elders and common elders below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall ceremony installed Three Elders and Five Worthies, with state and common elders below.

sentences.zh: 高祖再拜三老，親袒割牲，執爵而饋；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu twice bowed to the Three Elders, personally bared his shoulder, cut the sacrificial victim, and held the cup to feed them;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu twice bowed to the Three Elders, bared his shoulder, cut the victim, and fed them with his own hands;

sentences.zh: 於五更行肅拜之禮，賜國老、庶老衣服有差。

translations.literal: to the Five Worthies he performed the respectful bow, and bestowed robes on state and common elders in due ranks.
translations.idiomatic: he bowed to the Five Worthies and gave robes to the state and common elders.

sentences.zh: 既而元言曰：「自天地分判，五行施則，人之所崇，莫重於孝順。

translations.literal: Then Yuan said: "Since Heaven and Earth were divided and the Five Phases deployed, what men revere, nothing is heavier than filial obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then said that among human virtues filial obedience stood highest since Heaven and Earth were formed.

sentences.zh: 然五孝六順，天下之所先，願陛下重之，以化四方。

translations.literal: Yet the Five Filial Acts and Six Harmonious Ways are what the realm puts first; I wish Your Majesty to weight them to transform the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to weight the Five Filial and Six Harmonious teachings to transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣既衰老，不究遠趣，心耳所及，敢不盡誠。

translations.literal: Your servant is already aged and does not pursue distant aims; what heart and ear reach, I dare not fail in sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Though old and unable to pursue distant goals, he would speak with full sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「孝順之道，天地之經，今承三老明言，銘之于懷。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "The way of filial obedience is the warp of Heaven and Earth; now receiving the Three Elders' clear words, We inscribe them in Our breast."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu answered that filial obedience was Heaven and Earth's warp and vowed to keep Yuan's words in his heart.

sentences.zh: 」明根言曰：「夫至孝通靈，至順感幽，故詩云：孝悌之至，通於神明，光於四海。

translations.literal: Minggen said: "Supreme filial piety penetrates the spirits, supreme obedience moves the hidden—thus the Odes say: When filial piety and brotherliness reach their height, they penetrate to the spirits and shine over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen cited the Odes on filial piety reaching spirits and shining over the seas.

sentences.zh: [6]如此則孝順之道，無所不格。

translations.literal: [6] Thus the way of filial obedience has nowhere it does not reach.
translations.idiomatic: So filial obedience, he said, reached everywhere.

sentences.zh: 願陛下念之，以濟黎庶。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to keep it in mind to aid the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to remember this and aid the common people.

sentences.zh: 臣年志朽弊，識見昧然，在於心慮，不敢不盡。

translations.literal: Your servant's years and will are decayed, insight dim; in what the heart considers, I dare not fail to exhaust myself.
translations.idiomatic: Though his mind was dim with age, he would still speak fully.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「五更助三老以言至範，敷展德音，當克己復禮，以行來授。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "The Five Worthies assist the Three Elders in speaking the utmost pattern, spreading virtuous words; We should restrain Ourselves and return to ritual to carry out what you have granted."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told the Five Worthies that he would practice their teaching.

sentences.zh: 」禮畢，乃賜步挽一乘。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he bestowed one hand-drawn carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony ended he gave Yuan a hand-drawn carriage.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫尊老尚更，列聖同致；

translations.literal: An edict said: "To honor the aged and esteem the Worthies is what successive sage emperors alike reach;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that honoring elders and worthies united all sage rulers.

sentences.zh: 欽年敬德，綿哲齊軌。

translations.literal: to respect years and revere virtue is what sages of long antiquity alike follow.
translations.idiomatic: Revering age and virtue was the path of ancient sages.

sentences.zh: 朕雖道謝玄風，識昧叡則，仰禀先誨，企遵猷旨。

translations.literal: We, though the Way falls short of the mysterious wind and Our knowledge lacks the keen rule, receive the former teaching and look up to follow the intent of the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confessed his lesser virtue yet pledged to follow ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 故推老以德，立更以元，父焉斯彰，兄焉斯顯矣。

translations.literal: Therefore to push the aged by virtue and establish the Worthies by primacy makes the father thereby manifest and the elder brother thereby displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus elders were honored by virtue and Worthies by primacy, clarifying the roles of father and elder brother.

sentences.zh: 前司徒公元、前鴻臚卿明根並以沖德懸車，懿量歸老，故尊公以三，[7]事更以五。

translations.literal: The former Minister of Education Duke Yuan and the former Grand Herald Minggen, both with pure virtue suspending their carts and fine measure returning to age, were therefore honored—the Duke with the Three, [7] the Minister with the Five.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Minggen, both retired in pure virtue, were honored as Three Elder and Five Worthy.

sentences.zh: 雖更、老非官，耄耋罔祿，然況事既高，宜加殊養。

translations.literal: Though Worthy and Elder are not offices and the aged receive no salary, yet since the matter is lofty, special nurture should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Though these were not offices, their rank deserved special provision.

sentences.zh: 三老可給上公之祿，五更可食元卿之俸，供食之味，亦同其例。」

translations.literal: The Three Elders may be given the salary of the highest duke, the Five Worthies may eat the stipend of the primal ministers; the flavor of their provisions should follow the same example."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Elders received a highest duke's salary and the Five Worthies a prime minister's stipend, with commensurate fare.

sentences.zh: 子羽，名犯肅宗廟諱，頗有器望。

translations.literal: His son Yu had a name that violated Emperor Suzong's temple taboo and possessed considerable talent and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, whose name breached a temple taboo of Emperor Suzong, showed real promise.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書中散，駕部令，轉主客給事，加通直散騎常侍，守殿中尚書，兼侍中。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretariat Central Scribe, Chariot Office Director, transferred to Master of Guests Attendant, given the additional title Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, guarded the Palace Director of the Masters, and was also Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Secretariat scribe to Chariot Office director, Master of Guests attendant, Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 又起復本官，詔襲爵，加平南將軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled to his former post; an edict ordered him to inherit the title and gave the additional rank General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to office, he inherited the title and was named General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 高祖親考百司，以羽怠惰，降常侍為長兼，仍守尚書，奪祿一周。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu personally examined the hundred offices; because Yu was slack, he reduced the Cavalier Attendant to senior acting status, still guarding the Masters, and stripped one week's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's inspection found Yu slack; he was demoted to acting attendant, kept the Masters post, and fined a week's pay.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，以山陽在畿內，改為博陵郡開國公。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, because Shanyang lay within the inner circuit, the title was changed to Duke of Boling commandery with an open state.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang, Shanyang being in the inner circuit, the fief became Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 後為征虜將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，仍以為贈，諡曰順。

translations.literal: On death he was still given posthumous honors; his posthumous title was Shun.
translations.idiomatic: At death he received posthumous honors with the temple name Shun.

sentences.zh: 子景興，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingxing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 正始元年卒，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengshi he died; he was posthumously made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxing died in Zhengshi 1 and was posthumously named Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 景興弟景儁，襲爵。

translations.literal: Jingxing's younger brother Jingjun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jingjun inherited.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，坐杖國吏死，降封深澤縣開國公。

translations.literal: In Yanxing, because he beat a state clerk to death, he was reduced to Duke of Shenze commandery with an open state.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing he was reduced to Duke of Shenze for beating a government clerk to death.

sentences.zh: 子伯永，襲。

translations.literal: His son Boyong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boyong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Boyong had no son and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 羽弟靜，寬雅有才識。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Jing was easy and elegant, with talent and insight.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's brother Jing was cultured, talented, and discerning.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，為尚書左民郎中。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he was Left Bureau Director of the People in the Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he was Left Bureau Director of the People.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈博陵太守，重贈鎮軍將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Administrator of Boling; later again posthumously made General Who Guards the Army and Inspector of Luozhou, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Administrator of Boling, then General Who Guards the Army and Luozhou inspector, temple name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子祐之，通直散騎常侍、護軍長史。

translations.literal: His son Youzhi was Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Clerk of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youzhi was Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and chief clerk of the guards.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi died without further record.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜，慕容元真之玄孫。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao was the great-great-grandson of Murong Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao descended in the fourth generation from Murong Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 父琚，歷官以廉清著稱，賜爵高都侯。

translations.literal: His father Ju held office and was known for integrity and purity; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaodu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju won fame for clean government and was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaodu.

sentences.zh: 卒於冠軍將軍、尚書左丞，贈安南將軍、并州刺史、高都公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died as Champion General and Left Director of the Masters; posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Bingzhou, Duke of Gaodu, posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Ju died as Champion General and Left Director of the Masters and was posthumously General Who Pacifies the South, Bingzhou inspector, Duke of Gaodu, temple name Jian.

sentences.zh: 白曜少為中書吏，以敦直給事東宮。

translations.literal: Baiyao in youth was a Secretariat clerk; because of his honest uprightness he served in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Baiyao was a Secretariat clerk, then served the crown prince for his upright character.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，拜北部下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong acceded, he was appointed Lower Grandee of the Northern Department.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's accession he became Lower Grandee of the Northern Department.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，遷北部尚書。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was transferred to Director of the Northern Department.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and rose to Director of the Northern Department.

sentences.zh: 在職，執法無所阿縱，高宗厚待之。

translations.literal: In office he enforced the law without favoritism; Gaozong treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: In office he judged without partiality and Gaozong favored him.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，與乙渾共秉朝政，遷尚書右僕射，進爵南鄉公，加安南將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died he shared government with Yi Hun, was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters, advanced to Duke of Nanxiang, and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's death he shared power with Yi Hun, became Right Vice Director of the Masters, Duke of Nanxiang, and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 劉彧徐州刺史薛安都、兗州刺史畢眾敬並以城內附，詔鎮南大將軍尉元、鎮東將軍孔伯恭率師赴之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu and Inspector of Yanzhou Bi Zhongjing both submitted their cities; an edict ordered General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan and General Who Guards the East Kong Bogong to lead troops to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Andu and Bi Zhongjing submitted Xuzhou and Yanzhou, Wei Yuan and Kong Bogong were sent to receive them.

sentences.zh: 而彧東平太守申纂屯無鹽，并州刺史房崇吉屯升城，遏絕王使。

translations.literal: But Liu Yu's Administrator of Dongping Shen Zuan held Wuyan and the Inspector of Bingzhou Fang Chongji held Shengcheng, cutting off the royal envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shen Zuan held Wuyan and Fang Chongji held Shengcheng, blocking imperial envoys.

sentences.zh: 皇興初，加白曜使持節、都督諸軍事、征南大將軍、上黨公，屯於碻磝，以為諸軍後繼。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Baiyao was given the additional posts of credential-bearing commissioner, Commander-in-Chief of all armies, General Who Campaigns South, Duke of Shangdang, and encamped at Quepo as rear support for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing's opening year Baiyao was made campaign commander with full credentials, General Who Campaigns South, Duke of Shangdang, and camped at Quepo as army reserve.

sentences.zh: 白曜攻纂於無鹽城，拔其東郭。

translations.literal: Baiyao attacked Zuan at Wuyan city and took its eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao assaulted Zuan at Wuyan and seized the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 其夜纂遁，遣兵追執之，獲其男女數千口。

translations.literal: That night Zuan fled; troops were sent in pursuit and he was captured, along with several thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan fled that night, was caught in pursuit, and thousands of captives were taken.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉彧青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固並遣使內附，既而彧遣招慰，復歸於彧。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Yu's Inspector of Qingzhou Shen Wenxiu and Inspector of Jizhou Cui Daogu had both sent envoys to submit; afterward Liu Yu sent envoys to reassure them and they returned to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu had once submitted, but Liu Yu's envoys later won them back.

sentences.zh: 白曜既拔無鹽，回攻升城。

translations.literal: After Baiyao took Wuyan he turned to attack Shengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuyan fell Baiyao marched on Shengcheng.

sentences.zh: 肥城戍主聞軍至，棄城遁走，獲粟三十萬斛。

translations.literal: The garrison commander of Feicheng, hearing the army had arrived, abandoned the city and fled; thirty thousand hu of grain were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Feicheng's commander fled at his approach, leaving thirty thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 既至升城，垣苗、麋溝二戍拒守不下。

translations.literal: When he reached Shengcheng, the garrison commanders Yuan Miao and Mi Gou of the two forts resisted and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: At Shengcheng the commanders Yuan Miao and Mi Gou of two outworks held out and refused surrender.

sentences.zh: 白曜以千餘騎襲麋溝，麋溝潰，自投濟水死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Baiyao with more than a thousand horse raided Migou; Migou collapsed, and more than a thousand who threw themselves into the Ji River died.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao struck Migou with a thousand cavalry; the fort broke, and over a thousand drowned in the Ji.

sentences.zh: 擊垣苗，又破之，得粟十餘萬斛，由是軍糧充足。

translations.literal: He attacked Yuan Miao and broke him again, obtaining more than a hundred thousand hu of grain; thus army provisions were ample.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Yuan Miao as well and seized more than a hundred thousand hu of grain, fully supplying the army.

sentences.zh: 先是，淮陽公皮豹子等再征垣苗不克，白曜以一旬之內，頻拔四城，威震齊土。

translations.literal: Earlier the Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi and others had twice campaigned against Yuan Miao without success; Baiyao within ten days frequently took four cities, and his might shook Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Baozi had twice failed against Yuan Miao; Baiyao took four cities in ten days and awed all Qi.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘉焉，詔曰：「卿總率戎旅，討除不賓，霜戈所向，無不摧靡，旬日之內，克拔四城，韓白之功，何以加此？

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen was pleased and decreed: "You command the armies and punish the unsubmissive; wherever the frost spear points nothing fails to be shattered; within ten days four cities are seized—how can Han Xin's and Bai Qi's achievements surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen praised him for shattering rebels in ten days and asked what achievement could surpass Han Xin and Bai Qi.

sentences.zh: 雖升城戍將房崇吉守遠不順，危亡已形，潰在旦夕。

translations.literal: Though the Shengcheng garrison commander Fang Chongji holds far and will not submit, ruin is already shaped and collapse is within the dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Though Fang Chongji still held Shengcheng, his fall was already in sight.

sentences.zh: 宜勉崇威略，務存長轡，不必窮兵極武，以為勞頓。

translations.literal: You should encourage lofty strategy and keep the long reins; there is no need to exhaust troops and extreme force and thereby bring fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restraint, long-term strategy, and avoidance of exhausting the army.

sentences.zh: 且伐罪弔民，國之令典，當招懷以德，使來蘇之澤，加於百姓。

translations.literal: Moreover to punish crime and comfort the people is the state's constant canon; you should win them by virtue so that the blessing of renewal falls on the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He told Baiyao to punish wrongdoing yet comfort the people and win them with virtue.

sentences.zh: 」升城不降，白曜忿之，縱兵陵城，殺數百人，崇吉夜遁。

translations.literal: Shengcheng would not yield; Baiyao was angry, loosed troops to storm the city, killed several hundred, and Chongji fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengcheng refused surrender Baiyao stormed it, killed hundreds, and Chongji fled by night.

sentences.zh: 白曜撫慰其民，無所殺戮，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: Baiyao comforted the people and made no slaughter; the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He then soothed the populace without massacre, and they embraced him.

sentences.zh: 獲崇吉母妻，待之以禮。

translations.literal: He captured Chongji's mother and wife and treated them with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Chongji's mother and wife and treated them honorably.

sentences.zh: 劉彧遣其將吳憘公率眾數萬，欲寇彭城。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent his general Duke of Wu Xi with tens of thousands of men intending to invade Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Duke of Wu Xi with tens of thousands to threaten Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 鎮南大將軍尉元表請濟師。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan memorialized requesting reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan asked the throne for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 顯祖詔白曜赴之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen ordered Baiyao to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen ordered Baiyao to march to his aid.

sentences.zh: 白曜到瑕丘，遇患。

translations.literal: Baiyao reached Xiqiu and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao reached Xiqiu but fell sick.

sentences.zh: 時泗水暴竭，船不得進。

translations.literal: At the time the Si River suddenly dried and boats could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Si abruptly ran dry and boats could not pass.

sentences.zh: 憘公退，白曜因停瑕丘。

translations.literal: Xi withdrew, and Baiyao therefore halted at Xiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi retreated, and Baiyao remained at Xiqiu.

sentences.zh: 會崇吉與從弟法壽盜彧盤陽城以贖母妻。

translations.literal: Just then Chongji and his younger cousin Fashou stole Liu Yu's Panyang city to ransom mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji and his cousin Fashou seized Panyang to ransom their families.

sentences.zh: 白曜自瑕丘遣將軍長孫觀等率騎入自馬耳關赴之。

translations.literal: Baiyao from Xiqiu sent the general Zhangsun Guan and others with horse to enter through the Ma'er Pass to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiqiu he sent Zhangsun Guan through Ma'er Pass with cavalry to support them.

sentences.zh: 觀至盤陽，諸縣悉降。

translations.literal: When Guan reached Panyang, all the counties submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Panyang every county surrendered.

sentences.zh: 平東將軍長孫陵、寧東將軍尉眷東討青州，白曜自瑕丘進攻歷城。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the East Zhangsun Ling and General Who Pacifies the East Wei Juan campaigned east against Qingzhou; Baiyao from Xiqiu advanced to attack Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Ling and Wei Juan marched on Qingzhou while Baiyao advanced from Xiqiu against Licheng.

sentences.zh: 白曜乃為書以喻之曰：「天棄劉彧，禍難滋興，骨肉兄弟，自相誅戮，君臣上下，靡復紀綱。

translations.literal: Baiyao then wrote a letter to instruct them, saying: "Heaven has abandoned Liu Yu; disasters and hardships multiply; flesh-and-blood brothers slaughter one another; ruler and minister above and below no longer have discipline."
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao wrote to Licheng that Heaven had abandoned Liu Yu, kin were killing kin, and court order had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史薛安都、豫州刺史常珍奇、兗州刺史畢眾敬等深覩存亡，翻然歸義。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu, Inspector of Yuzhou Chang Zhenqi, Inspector of Yanzhou Bi Zhongjing, and others deeply saw survival and ruin and suddenly turned to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu, Chang Zhenqi, Bi Zhongjing, and others had already seen which way survival lay and submitted.

sentences.zh: 故朝廷納其誠欵，委以南蕃。

translations.literal: Therefore the court accepted their sincere pledge and entrusted them with the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The court had accepted their loyalty and entrusted the southern marches to them.

sentences.zh: 皆目前之見事，東西所備聞也。

translations.literal: All are present matters before the eyes, heard in east and west alike.
translations.idiomatic: These were recent facts known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 彼無鹽戍主申纂敢縱姦慝，劫奪行人，官軍始臨，一時授首。

translations.literal: The Wuyan garrison commander Shen Zuan dared indulge wickedness, plundering travelers; when the official army first arrived he at once lost his head.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuan of Wuyan had plundered travelers and fell the moment imperial troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 房崇吉固守升城，尋即潰散。

translations.literal: Fang Chongji firmly held Shengcheng but soon collapsed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Chongji had held Shengcheng only to see it swiftly break apart.

sentences.zh: 自襄陽以東，至于淮海，莫不風靡，服從正化。

translations.literal: From Xiangyang east to the Huai and sea, none failed to bend before the wind and submit to correct transformation.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiangyang to the Huai coast all had bowed to Wei's civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 謂東陽、歷城有識之士，上思安都之榮顯，下念申纂之死亡，追悔前惑，改圖後悟。

translations.literal: I say that the men of insight in Dongyang and Licheng, thinking above of Andu's glory and splendor and below of Zuan's death, should repent former delusion and change their plan in later awakening.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Dongyang and Licheng should recall Andu's honors and Zuan's death, repent, and turn.

sentences.zh: 然執守愚迷，不能自革。

translations.literal: Yet you cling to obstinate folly and cannot reform yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they clung to folly and would not change.

sentences.zh: 猥總戎旅，掃定北方。

translations.literal: I have presumptuously gathered the armies and swept the north settled.
translations.idiomatic: I have swept the north with the imperial host.

sentences.zh: 濟黃河知十二之虛說，臨齊境想一變之清風，踟躕周覽，依然何極。

translations.literal: Crossing the Yellow River I know the empty tale of the Twelve; approaching Qi territory I think of the clear wind of a single change—hesitating, looking all around, how endless it remains.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yellow River I see through empty boasts; entering Qi I await a change of heart—yet you hesitate without end.

sentences.zh: 故先馳書，以喻成敗。

translations.literal: Therefore I first send this letter to show success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: I send this letter first to show you triumph and ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫見機而動，周易所稱；

translations.literal: To see the moment and act is what the Book of Changes praises;
translations.idiomatic: The Changes praise acting when the moment appears;

sentences.zh: 去危就安，人事常理。

translations.literal: to leave danger and seek safety is the constant reason of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: leaving danger for safety is human nature's rule.

sentences.zh: 若以一介為高，不悛為美，則微子負嫌於時，紀季受譏於世。

translations.literal: If you take one stubborn stand as lofty and not repenting as beautiful, then Weizi bore blame in his time and Ji Ji received ridicule in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn loyalty made Weizi and Ji Ji objects of scorn in their own ages.

sentences.zh: 我皇魏重光累葉，德懷無外，軍威所拂，無不披靡。

translations.literal: Our august Wei has repeated glory through successive leaves, virtue embracing all beyond the borders; where military might brushes, none fails to be overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei shines through generations; where its armies pass, none stand.

sentences.zh: 固非三吳弱卒所能擬抗。

translations.literal: It is truly not something the weak soldiers of the Three Wu can match and resist.
translations.idiomatic: The feeble troops of Wu cannot withstand this.

sentences.zh: 況於今者，勢已土崩。

translations.literal: Moreover as of now the situation has already collapsed like earth.
translations.idiomatic: Now your state has already crumbled.

sentences.zh: 劉彧威不制秣陵，政不出閫外，豈復能浮江越海，赴危救急。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's might does not control Moling; government does not go beyond the outer gate—how could he again float across the Yangtze and sea to rush to danger and save urgency?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu cannot rule beyond his capital, much less cross the Yangtze to save you.

sentences.zh: 恃此為援，何異於蹄涔之魚，冀拯江海。

translations.literal: Relying on this as aid—how is it different from fish in a hoofprint hoping to be saved by the rivers and sea?
translations.idiomatic: To rely on him is like a puddle fish hoping for the ocean.

sentences.zh: 夫蝮蛇螫手則斷手，螫足則斷足，誠忍肌體以救性命。

translations.literal: When the viper stings the hand one cuts off the hand; when it stings the foot one cuts off the foot—truly one endures cutting flesh to save life.
translations.idiomatic: When a viper stings hand or foot, the wise cut off the limb to save life.

sentences.zh: 若推義而行之，無割身之痛也，而可以保家寧宗，長守安樂。

translations.literal: If you push righteousness and act, there is no pain of cutting the body, yet you can preserve the family, settle the clan, and long keep peace and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Act with righteousness and you need not maim yourself yet may keep your house at peace.

sentences.zh: 此智士所宜深思重慮，自求多福。」

translations.literal: This is what men of wisdom should deeply ponder and weigh, seeking much blessing for themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Wise men should ponder this and choose blessing for themselves."

sentences.zh: 道固固守不降，白曜築長圍以攻之。

translations.literal: Daogu firmly held and would not yield; Baiyao built a long encirclement to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Daogu held out; Baiyao invested the city with a long siege.

sentences.zh: 長孫陵等既至青州，沈文秀遣使請降。

translations.literal: When Zhangsun Ling and the rest reached Qingzhou, Shen Wenxiu sent an envoy to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingzhou Shen Wenxiu first sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 軍人入其西郛，頗有採掠，文秀悔之，遂嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: Soldiers entered the western suburb and there was considerable plundering; Wenxiu regretted it and then girded the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Troops plundered his western suburb; Wenxiu repented and shut the gates to resist.

sentences.zh: 二年，崔道固及兗州刺史梁鄒守將劉休賓並面縛而降。

translations.literal: In the second year Cui Daogu and the Liangzou garrison commander Liu Xiubin of Yanzhou Inspector both came bound to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In year two Cui Daogu and Liu Xiubin of Liangzou came bound in surrender.

sentences.zh: 白曜皆釋而禮之。

translations.literal: Baiyao released them all and treated them with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao freed them and treated them with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 送道固、休賓及其僚屬于京師。

translations.literal: He sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their staffs to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their staffs to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後乃徙二城民望於下館，朝廷置平齊郡，懷寧、歸安二縣以居之。

translations.literal: Afterward he moved the leading families of the two cities to Xiaguan; the court established Pingqi commandery with Huaining and Gui'an counties to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Leading families of both cities were moved to Xiaguan under the new Pingqi commandery with Huaining and Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 自餘悉為奴婢，分賜百官。

translations.literal: The rest were all made slaves and maidservants and distributed to the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder were enslaved and given to officials.

sentences.zh: 白曜雖在軍旅，而接待人物，寬和有禮。

translations.literal: Though Baiyao was in the army, in receiving people he was easy and had ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Even in camp Baiyao received people with ease and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 獲崇吉母妻、申纂婦女，皆別營安置，不令士卒諠雜。

translations.literal: Capturing Chongji's mother and wife and Zuan's women, he separately encamped and settled them and did not let the soldiers make clamor.
translations.idiomatic: He housed Chongji's and Zuan's families apart and kept soldiers from harassing them.

sentences.zh: 乃進討東陽。

translations.literal: He then advanced to attack Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，入其西郭。

translations.literal: In winter he entered the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he entered Dongyang's western suburb.

sentences.zh: 三年春，克東陽，擒沈文秀。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he took Dongyang and captured Shen Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's spring he took Dongyang and seized Shen Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 凡獲倉粟八十五萬斛，米三千斛，弓九千張，箭十八萬八千，刀二萬二千四百，甲冑各三千三百，銅五千斤，錢十五萬；

translations.literal: In all he captured granary grain of eight hundred fifty thousand hu, rice three thousand hu, bows nine thousand, arrows one hundred eighty-eight thousand, knives twenty-two thousand four hundred, armor three thousand three hundred each, copper five thousand jin, and cash one hundred fifty thousand;
translations.idiomatic: The booty included 850,000 hu of grain, 9,000 bows, 188,000 arrows, 22,400 knives, 3,300 suits of armor, and 150,000 cash;

sentences.zh: 城內戶八千六百，口四萬一千，吳蠻戶三百餘。

translations.literal: within the city eight thousand six hundred households, forty-one thousand mouths, and more than three hundred Wu barbarian households.
translations.idiomatic: the city held 8,600 households, 41,000 people, and 300-odd Wu barbarian families.

sentences.zh: 始末三年，築圍攻擊，日日交兵，雖士卒死傷，無多怨叛。

translations.literal: From beginning to end three years, building encirclements and attacking, fighting day by day—though soldiers died and were wounded, there was not much resentment or rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: For three years of daily fighting, though men fell, few turned mutinous.

sentences.zh: 督上土人租絹，以為軍資，不至侵苦。

translations.literal: He supervised the local people's land tax in silk as army provisions and did not reach oppression and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: He levied local silk taxes for supplies without oppressing the people.

sentences.zh: 三齊欣然，安堵樂業。

translations.literal: The Three Qi were pleased; they settled in peace and rejoiced in their work.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Qi submitted gladly and lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 克城之日，以沈文秀抗倨不為之拜，忿而箠撻，唯以此見譏。

translations.literal: On the day the city was taken, because Shen Wenxiu resisted arrogantly and would not bow to him, he was angry and flogged him—only in this was he criticized.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiu refused to bow he flogged him—the only act for which he was criticized.

sentences.zh: 以功拜使持節、都督青齊東徐州諸軍事、開府儀同三司、青州刺史、濟南王，將軍如故。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed credential-bearing commissioner, Commander-in-Chief of Qing, Qi, and Eastern Xuzhou, Equal in Office to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Qingzhou, Prince of Jinan, with general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he became commander of Qing, Qi, and Eastern Xu, equal to the Three Excellencies, Qingzhou inspector, and Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 四年冬見誅。

translations.literal: In the fourth winter he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year's winter he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 初乙渾專權，白曜頗所俠附，緣此追以為責。

translations.literal: Earlier when Yi Hun monopolized power, Baiyao had rather leaned on him; because of this he was later pursued as culpable.
translations.idiomatic: He had leaned on Yi Hun's faction, which later counted against him.

sentences.zh: 及將誅也，云謀反叛，時論冤之。

translations.literal: When he was about to be executed they said he plotted rebellion; opinion at the time called it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with rebellion at his death, which contemporaries deemed unjust.

sentences.zh: 白曜少子真安，年十一，聞父被執，將自殺。

translations.literal: Baiyao's youngest son Zhen'an, age eleven, heard his father was seized and was about to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: His eleven-year-old son Zhen'an, hearing his father was arrested, tried to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 家人止之，曰：「輕重未可知。

translations.literal: The family stopped him, saying: "The gravity is not yet known."
translations.idiomatic: His family stopped him, saying the outcome was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 」真安曰：「王位高功重，若有小罪，終不至此。

translations.literal: Zhen'an said: "The princely rank is high and merit weighty; if there were a small crime, in the end it would not come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'an replied that a prince of such merit would not be ruined for a small fault.

sentences.zh: 我何忍見父之死。

translations.literal: How could I bear to see my father's death?"
translations.idiomatic: He could not bear to see his father die."

sentences.zh: 」遂自縊焉。

translations.literal: He then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 白曜弟如意，亦從白曜平歷下，與白曜同誅。

translations.literal: Baiyao's younger brother Ruyi had also followed Baiyao in pacifying Lixia and was executed with Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ruyi, who had helped pacify Lixia, was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 太和中，著作佐郎成淹上表理白曜曰：

translations.literal: In Taihe, the Editorial Assistant Cheng Yan submitted a memorial to vindicate Baiyao, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe, Editorial Assistant Cheng Yan memorialized to vindicate Baiyao:

sentences.zh: 臣聞經疆啟宇，實良將之功；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that opening borders and founding domains is truly the achievement of good generals;
translations.idiomatic: Opening borders, he wrote, was the work of great generals;
