sentences.zh: 褒德酬庸，乃聖王之務。

translations.literal: praising virtue and repaying merit is the business of sage kings.
translations.idiomatic: rewarding merit was the duty of sage kings.

sentences.zh: 昔姜公杖鉞，開隆周之基；

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Jiang took the battle-axe and opened the foundation of flourishing Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Taigong took the axe and founded Zhou;

sentences.zh: 韓生秉旄，興鴻漢之業。

translations.literal: Han Xin held the banner and raised the soaring Han enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin raised the banner and built Han.

sentences.zh: 故能賞超當時，名垂前史。

translations.literal: Therefore rewards surpassed their age and names hang in former histories.
translations.idiomatic: Their rewards and names outlasted their ages.

sentences.zh: 若閫外功成，而流言內作，人主猜疑，良將懷懼，樂毅所以背燕，章邯所以奔楚。

translations.literal: If merit beyond the gates succeeds while slander works within, the ruler grows suspicious and good generals harbor fear—Yue Yi therefore turned his back on Yan, Zhang Han therefore fled to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When court slander follows frontier victory, rulers grow suspicious and generals flee, as with Yue Yi and Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 至如鄧艾懷忠，矯命寧國，赤心皎然，幽顯同見，而橫受屠戮，良可悲哀。

translations.literal: As for Deng Ai, he cherished loyalty and bent orders to settle the state; his red heart was bright, hidden and manifest alike seen—yet he was cut down across the board, truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai served loyally yet was slaughtered—a pitiable case.

sentences.zh: 及士治伐吳，[9]奮不顧命，萬里浮江，應機直指，使孫皓君臣，輿櫬入洛。

translations.literal: And when Wang Jun campaigned against Wu, [9] he strove without regard for life, floated on the river ten thousand li, aimed straight at the moment, and made Sun Hao's ruler and ministers come in carts to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, ignoring death, sailed ten thousand li and brought Sun Hao to Luoyang in surrender.

sentences.zh: 大功亦舉，讒書驟至，內外唱和，貝錦將成，微晉武之鑒，亦幾於顛沛矣。

translations.literal: Great merit was also achieved, but slanderous letters suddenly arrived; inside and outside sang together, brocade slander was about to be woven—without Jin Wu's discernment he too would nearly have been overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Yet slander nearly destroyed Wang Jun until Jin Wu saw through it.

sentences.zh: 每覽其事，常為痛心，聖主明王，固宜深察。

translations.literal: Whenever I read these affairs I am constantly pained at heart; sage rulers and bright kings should indeed examine deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Reading such cases pains me; sage rulers must judge more deeply.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見故征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、青州刺史、濟南王慕容白曜，祖父相資，世酋東裔，值皇運廓被，委節臣妾。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully sees the former General Who Campaigns South, Equal in Office to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Qingzhou, Prince of Jinan Murong Baiyao: grandfather and father each supported the other, chieftains for generations in the eastern borderlands; when the imperial fortune broadly covered them, they entrusted their allegiance as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao's line had served as eastern chieftains and long submitted when the imperial fortune spread.

sentences.zh: 白曜生長王國，飲服道教，爵列上階，位登帝伯。

translations.literal: Baiyao grew up in the royal domain, drank and wore the Way's teaching, rank in the upper steps, position reaching imperial peer.
translations.idiomatic: He grew in the royal domain, rose to the highest ranks, and stood among the empire's peers.

sentences.zh: [10]去天安初，江陰夷楚，敢拒王命，三方阻兵，連城岳峙。

translations.literal: [10] From the beginning of Tian'an, the Yi and Chu of Jiangyin dared resist the royal command; three directions blocked with troops, linked cities standing like peaks.
translations.idiomatic: From Tian'an onward the south resisted, cities linked like mountains.

sentences.zh: 海岱蒼生，翹首拯援。

translations.literal: The black-haired people of the sea and Dai looked up for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the coast looked up for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 聖朝乃眷南顧，思救荒黎，大議廟堂，顯舉元將，百僚同音，僉曰惟允。

translations.literal: The holy court then turned its gaze south, thinking to save the suffering masses; great deliberation in the temple hall, clearly raising the primal general—all offices with one voice, all saying he alone was fit.
translations.idiomatic: The court turned south, chose a supreme commander, and every office agreed on Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 遂推轂委誠，授以專征之任，握兵十萬，杖鉞一方。

translations.literal: Thereupon pushing the chariot wheel they entrusted sincerity, granting the power of special campaign, holding a hundred thousand troops and leaning on the battle-axe in one region.
translations.idiomatic: He received full command with a hundred thousand men and the battle-axe of one region.

sentences.zh: 威陵河濟則淮徐震懼，師出無鹽而申纂授首。

translations.literal: His might overawed the He and Ji so Huai and Xu trembled in fear; the army left Wuyan and Shen Zuan lost his head.
translations.idiomatic: His might shook the He and Ji; at Wuyan Shen Zuan lost his head.

sentences.zh: 濟北、太原，同時消潰；

translations.literal: Jibei and Taiyuan collapsed at the same time;
translations.idiomatic: Jibei and Taiyuan fell together;

sentences.zh: 麋溝、垣苗，相尋奔走。

translations.literal: Migou and Yuan Miao fled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Migou and Yuan Miao fled one after another.

sentences.zh: 及回麾東掃，道固銜璧，盤陽、梁鄒，肉袒請命。

translations.literal: When he turned his banner east to sweep, Daogu offered his jade disk, Panyang and Liangzou bared their torsos and begged for life.
translations.idiomatic: Turning east, Daogu surrendered, and Panyang and Liangzou came bound.

sentences.zh: 于時東陽未平，人懷去就。

translations.literal: At that time Dongyang was not yet pacified; men's hearts wavered between going and staying.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyang still held out and hearts wavered.

sentences.zh: 沈文靜、高崇仁擁眾不朝，扇擾邊服。

translations.literal: Shen Wenjing and Gao Chongren held masses and would not attend court, stirring and disturbing the border service.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenjing and Gao Chongren held troops and refused court.

sentences.zh: 崔僧祐、蓋次陽、陳顯達連兵淮海，水陸鋒起，揚旌而至，規援青齊。

translations.literal: Cui Sengyou, Gai Ciyang, and Chen Xianda linked armies on the Huai and sea; on water and land spears rose, they raised banners and came, planning to relieve Qing and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Sengyou, Gai Ciyang, and Chen Xianda marched on the Huai to relieve Qing and Qi.

sentences.zh: 士民汹汹，莫不南顧。

translations.literal: Officers and people were in uproar; none failed to look south.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and people looked anxiously southward.

sentences.zh: 時兵役既久，咸有歸心，而白曜外宣皇風，內盡方略，身擐甲冑，與士卒同，安撫初附，示以恩厚。

translations.literal: At that time military service had been long; all had hearts of return, yet Baiyao outwardly proclaimed the imperial wind and inwardly exhausted strategy, personally donning armor in the same lot as the soldiers, soothing those first submitted and showing them deep kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Though troops longed for home, Baiyao wore armor with them, proclaimed imperial virtue, and gently settled new subjects.

sentences.zh: 三軍懷挾纊之溫，新民欣來蘇之澤。

translations.literal: The three armies cherished the warmth of hugging cotton; the new subjects rejoiced in the blessing of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers felt cared for; new subjects felt the blessing of renewal.

sentences.zh: 遂使僧祐擁徒弭旆，効順軍門；

translations.literal: Thereupon Sengyou gathered his followers and lowered his banners, submitting in effect at the army gate;
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou then lowered his banners and submitted at the camp gate;

sentences.zh: 文靜、崇仁棄城竄海；

translations.literal: Wenjing and Chongren abandoned the city and fled to the sea;
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing and Chongren fled by sea;

sentences.zh: 次陽、顯達望塵南奔。

translations.literal: Ciyang and Xianda fled south at the sight of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Ciyang and Xianda ran south at the first rumor of defeat.

sentences.zh: 聲震江吳，風偃荊漢。

translations.literal: The sound shook the Yangtze and Wu; the wind laid low Jing and Han.
translations.idiomatic: His fame shook the lower Yangtze and humbled the Han riverlands.

sentences.zh: 及青州克平，文秀面縛，海波清靜，三齊克定，逖彼東南，永為國有。

translations.literal: When Qingzhou was pacified and taken, Wenxiu came bound; the sea waves grew quiet; the Three Qi were settled; that southeastern land became forever the state's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou fell, Wenxiu was bound, the sea grew calm, the Three Qi were settled, and the southeast became imperial territory.

sentences.zh: 使天府納六州之貢，濟泗息烽警之虞，開岱宗封禪之略，闢山川望秩之序。

translations.literal: He made the celestial storehouse receive the tribute of six provinces, the Ji and Si cease the worry of beacon fires, opened the plan of feng and shan on Mount Dai, and established the order of mountain and river sacrifices by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial storehouses filled with tribute from six provinces, beacon fires on the Ji and Si died out, and the rites of Tai and the ranked sacrifices were restored.

sentences.zh: 斯誠宗廟之靈，神算所授，然抑亦白曜與有力矣。

translations.literal: This is truly the numen of the ancestral temple and a gift of divine calculation—yet it must also be said that Baiyao had a share of the force.
translations.idiomatic: It was the ancestral temple's blessing and Heaven's plan—yet Baiyao had borne no small part.

sentences.zh: 及氛翳既靜，爵命亦隆，榮燭當時，聲譽日遠。

translations.literal: When the miasma and cover had grown quiet, rank and command also rose high; glory illuminated the age and reputation spread daily afar.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned his honors mounted and his fame spread far.

sentences.zh: 而民惡其上，妄生尤隙，因其功高，流言惑聽。

translations.literal: Yet the people hated their superiors and recklessly bore grievances; because his merit was high, floating words confused the listeners.
translations.idiomatic: Yet malcontents slandered him, and because his merit was great rumor swayed the court.

sentences.zh: 巧偽亂真，朱紫難辨，傷夷未瘳，合門屠戮。

translations.literal: Crafty falsehood confused truth, cinnabar and purple were hard to distinguish; wounds and ruin were not yet healed when the whole household was slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Slander confused truth; before wounds had healed his whole house was slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 鴻勳盛德，蔑爾無聞。

translations.literal: Grand merit and flourishing virtue were scorned and unheard.
translations.idiomatic: His great merit and virtue were erased.

sentences.zh: 有識之徒，能不悽愴。

translations.literal: Men of insight—who could fail to be deeply grieved?
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful men could only grieve.

sentences.zh: 臣謂白曜策名王庭，累荷榮授，歷司出內，世載忠美。

translations.literal: Your servant says Baiyao made his name in the royal court, repeatedly bore honored appointments, passed through offices inside and out, and for generations carried loyal beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao had served the throne for generations with loyal distinction.

sentences.zh: 秉鉞啟蕃，折衝敵國，開疆千里，拔城十二，辛勤於戎旅之際，契闊於矢石之間，登鋒履危，志存靜亂。

translations.literal: He held the battle-axe and opened the frontier, broke the enemy state, opened a thousand li of border, took twelve cities, toiled amid the armies, was bound in hardship between arrows and stones, mounted the spearhead and trod danger, his will set on quelling turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a thousand li, took twelve cities, shared hardship with his troops, and sought only to pacify chaos.

sentences.zh: 及方難既夷，身膺高賞，受胙河山，與國昇降，六十之年，寵靈已極。

translations.literal: When the square difficulty was already pacified he personally received high reward, received fief on river and mountain, rose and fell with the state—in sixty years favor and numen had already reached the limit.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he received a great fief and sixty years of honors at the state's side.

sentences.zh: 觀其立功，足明機運，豈容僥倖，更邀非望者乎？

translations.literal: Viewing his establishment of merit, it is enough to show the turn of opportunity—how could he tolerate chance and seek further improper hope?
translations.idiomatic: His merit showed Heaven's favor; how could he have sought more?

sentences.zh: 且於時，國家士馬，屯積京南，跨州連鎮，勢侔雲岳。

translations.literal: Moreover at that time the state's soldiers and horses were massed south of the capital; provinces and garrisons linked across the land, their momentum like cloud-capped peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial armies massed south of the capital, province linked to province, their strength like mountains.

sentences.zh: 主將驍雄，按鉀在所，莫不殉忠死難，効節奉時。

translations.literal: Chief generals were fierce and heroic; wherever armor was set, none failed to die loyal for principle and show integrity in serving the age.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce commanders stood ready everywhere, each willing to die for the throne.

sentences.zh: 此之不可生心，白曜足知之矣。

translations.literal: That one must not harbor such a heart—Baiyao knew it well enough.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao knew well that rebellion was impossible.

sentences.zh: 況潛逆阻兵，營岱厭亂，加以王師仍舉，州郡屠裂，齊民勞止，神膽俱喪，亡燼之眾不可與圖存，離敗之民不可與語勇哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the hidden rebel blocked troops, garrisoned Dai and wearied of turmoil; add to that the royal army still campaigning, provinces and commanderies torn apart, Qi people laboring and resting, spirits and gall all lost—the people of dead embers cannot be plotted with for survival, the people of scattered defeat cannot be spoken with for courage!
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were crushed, provinces ravaged, Qi lay exhausted, and broken men could neither fight nor plot.

sentences.zh: 白曜果毅習戎，體閑兵勢，寧不知士民之不可藉，將士之不同己，據強兵之勢，因塗炭之民，而欲立非常之事，此愚夫之所弗為也。

translations.literal: Baiyao was resolute and practiced in arms, understood military momentum—how could he not know the officers and people could not be relied on, that officers and soldiers were not of one mind with him, and yet rely on strong troops' momentum and exploit a people in charcoal to desire establishing an extraordinary affair? This is what the foolish husband would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao knew soldiers and people would not follow a revolt and that only a fool would exploit ruin to rebel.

sentences.zh: 料此推之，事可知矣。

translations.literal: Deducing from this, the affair can be known.
translations.idiomatic: From this the truth is clear.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下聖鑒自天，仁孝宰世，風冠宇宙，道超百王。

translations.literal: Your servant bows that Your Majesty's sage mirror comes from Heaven, benevolence and filial piety rule the age, wind crowns the universe, the Way surpasses the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's wisdom surpasses all kings, your benevolence rules the age.

sentences.zh: 開國以來，諸有罪犯極刑，不得骸骨者，悉聽收葬。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the state, all who committed crimes deserving extreme punishment and could not receive bones—all were permitted burial.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding, even men executed for grave crimes have been allowed burial.

sentences.zh: 大造之恩，振古未有。

translations.literal: The grace of great creation has never been matched in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Such grace is unmatched in history.

sentences.zh: 而白曜人舊功高，嬰禍淪覆，名滅國除，爵命無紹。

translations.literal: Yet Baiyao was an old servant of high merit who met disaster and was overthrown; his name was extinguished and the state removed; rank and command had no succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Baiyao, though old and meritorious, was destroyed without heirs or rank.

sentences.zh: 天下眾庶，咸共哀憐，方之餘流，應有差異。

translations.literal: All under Heaven, the many and the base, together mourned and pitied him; compared with other streams there should be a difference.
translations.idiomatic: All the realm pitied him and asked mercy for his line.

sentences.zh: 願陛下揚日月之光，明勳臣之績，垂天地之施，慰僵屍之魂。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to raise the sun and moon's light, make clear the merit of meritorious subjects, extend Heaven and Earth's favor, and comfort the souls of the stiff corpses.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty shine sun and moon on his merit and comfort the dead.

sentences.zh: 使合棺定諡，歿有餘稱。

translations.literal: Let the coffin be closed and the posthumous title fixed, so that in death he has surplus praise.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him coffin, title, and posthumous praise.

sentences.zh: 選其宗近，才堪驅策，錫以微爵，繼其絕世。

translations.literal: Choose from his clan those near in kin who have talent fit for driving and service; bestow a slight rank and continue his severed age.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a worthy kinsman, give a modest title, and continue his line.

sentences.zh: 進可以奬勸將來，退可以顯國恩澤。

translations.literal: Advancing can encourage and warn the future; retreating can display the state's grace and favor.
translations.idiomatic: This would reward the living and honor the dead while displaying imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 使存者荷莫大之恩，死者受骨肉之惠，豈不美哉！

translations.literal: Let the living bear measureless grace and the dead receive flesh-and-blood kindness—is it not beautiful?
translations.idiomatic: The living would be boundlessly grateful and the dead kindly remembered—how beautiful!

sentences.zh: 仰惟聖明，霈然昭覽，狂瞽之言，伏待刑憲。

translations.literal: Looking up to your sage clarity, may you brightly survey; the words of this mad blind man await punishment by law.
translations.idiomatic: I submit these rash words for your judgment and punishment if I err.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽表，嘉愍之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu read the memorial and was pleased and moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the memorial and was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 白曜弟子契，輕薄無檢。

translations.literal: Baiyao's nephew Qi was frivolous and without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao's nephew Qi was frivolous and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 太和初，以名家子擢為中散，遷宰官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, as a son of an eminent house he was promoted to Central Scribe and transferred to Director of the Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe this scion of a great house rose to Central Scribe and Director of the Masters.

sentences.zh: 南安王楨有貪暴之響，遣中散閭文祖詣長安察之。

translations.literal: Prince of Nan'an Zhen had a reputation for greedy violence; he sent Central Scribe Lü Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nan'an Zhen was known for greed; the court sent Lü Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate.

sentences.zh: 文祖受楨金寶之賂，為楨隱而不言。

translations.literal: Wenzu received Zhen's bribe of gold and treasures and concealed it for Zhen without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzu took Zhen's gold and concealed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 事發，坐之。

translations.literal: When the affair broke out, he was punished for it.
translations.idiomatic: When exposed he was punished.

sentences.zh: 文明太后引見羣臣，謂之曰：「前論貪清，皆云克修，文祖時亦在中，後竟犯法。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming received the ministers and said to them: "Earlier when we discussed greed and purity, all said they could cultivate themselves; Wenzu was then also among them, yet afterward he finally violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming told the court that Wenzu, though once praised for integrity, had proved corrupt.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，人心信不可知。

translations.literal: From this speaking, the human heart truly cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: From this, she said, the human heart cannot be known."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「古有待放之臣，亦有離俗之士，卿等自審不勝貪心者，聽辭位歸第。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "In antiquity there were ministers awaiting dismissal and also men leaving the vulgar; you yourselves examine whether you cannot overcome greedy hearts—hear and resign your posts and return to your mansions."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said that any who feared greed should resign and go home.

sentences.zh: 」契進曰：「臣卑微小人，聞識不遠，過蒙曲照，虛忝令職。

translations.literal: Qi advanced and said: "Your servant is a lowly petty man; hearing and knowledge do not reach far; I excessively received your bent illumination and vainly occupy this fine office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied that he was a petty man unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 小人之心無定，帝王之法有常。

translations.literal: The petty man's heart has no fixity; the august emperor's law has constancy.
translations.idiomatic: A petty heart cannot keep constant law.

sentences.zh: 以無恒之心，奉有常之法，非所克堪。

translations.literal: With an inconstant heart to serve constant law is not what one can bear.
translations.idiomatic: He could not serve constant law with an inconstant heart.

sentences.zh: 乞垂退免。

translations.literal: I beg you to grant dismissal and removal."
translations.idiomatic: He begged to be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「昔鄭相嗜魚，人有獻魚者，相曰『若取此魚，恐削名祿』，遂不肯受。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Formerly the prime minister of Zheng loved fish; a man presented fish and the minister said, 'If I take this fish I fear my name and salary will be cut,' and therefore would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu cited the Zheng minister who refused fish lest he grow greedy.

sentences.zh: 契若知心不可常，即知貪之惡矣，何為求退？

translations.literal: If Qi knows the heart cannot be constant, then he knows the evil of greed—why seek dismissal?"
translations.idiomatic: If Qi knew his heart was inconstant, Gaozu said, he already knew greed's evil—why resign?

sentences.zh: 」遷宰官令，微好碎事，頗曉工作，主司厨宰，稍以見知。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters; he slightly liked trifling affairs and understood workmanship rather well; the chief office for kitchens and slaughter gradually came to know him.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Masters, showed skill in practical work, and won notice in the kitchen offices.

sentences.zh: 及營洛陽基構，征新野、南陽起諸攻具，契皆參典。

translations.literal: When the Luoyang foundations were laid and Xinye and Nanyang were levied for siege engines, Qi participated in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was built and siege engines were raised in Xinye and Nanyang, Qi took part.

sentences.zh: 太和末，以功遷太中大夫、光祿少卿、營州大中正，賜爵定陶男。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe, for merit he was transferred to Grand Palace Doctor, Vice Director of the Imperial Household, Chief Rectifier of Yingzhou, and enfeoffed as Baron of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taihe he became Grand Palace Doctor, Vice Director of the Imperial Household, Yingzhou chief rectifier, and Baron of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除征虜將軍、營州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi's opening year he became General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Yingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 徙都督沃野、薄骨律二鎮諸軍事，沃野鎮將，轉都督禦夷、懷荒二鎮諸軍事，平城鎮將，將軍並如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Commander-in-Chief of the Woye and Bogulü garrisons, General of Woye Garrison, then transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the Yiyi and Huaihuang garrisons, General of Pingcheng Garrison, with general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the Woye and Bogulü garrisons, then the Yiyi and Huaihuang garrisons, keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 轉都督朔州、沃野懷朔武川三鎮三道諸軍事，後將軍，朔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the three routes of Shuozhou and the Woye, Huaishuo, and Wuchuan garrisons, Rear General, Inspector of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded Shuozhou and three frontier routes as Rear General and Shuozhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年卒，贈鎮北將軍、并州刺史，諡曰克。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping he died; posthumously he was made General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Bingzhou, posthumous title Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xiping 1 and was posthumously General Who Guards the North, Bingzhou inspector, temple name Ke.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容破後，種族仍繁。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Murong polity was broken, the clan remained numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong's fall the clan remained numerous.

sentences.zh: 天賜末，頗忌而誅之。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianxi they were much feared and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianxi's end many were feared and executed.

sentences.zh: 時有遺免，不敢復姓，皆以「輿」為氏。

translations.literal: At that time there were survivors who dared not resume the surname; all took the surname Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors dared not use the Murong surname and took Yu instead.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，詔復舊姓，而其子女先入掖庭者，猶號慕容，特多於他族。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanxing an edict restored the old surname, but those sons and daughters who had earlier entered the rear court still were called Murong—especially many among other clans.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxing restored the surname, though palace women still bore Murong, more than other lines.

sentences.zh: 契長子昇，字僧度。

translations.literal: Qi's eldest son Sheng, style name Sengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's eldest son was Sheng, style name Sengdu.

sentences.zh: 建興太守，遷鎮遠將軍、沃野鎮將，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Administrator of Jianxing, transferred to General Who Pacifies the Distance and General of Woye Garrison, advanced in title to General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was Administrator of Jianxing, then General Who Pacifies the Distance and Woye garrison commander, then General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 甚得邊民情。

translations.literal: He greatly won the frontier people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply won the frontier people's trust.

sentences.zh: 和第二子僧濟，[11]自奉朝請稍轉至五校。

translations.literal: He and Qi's second son Sengji, [11] from Court Attendant gradually rose to the Five Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's second son Sengji rose from Court Attendant to the Five Commandants.

sentences.zh: 耽淫酒色，不事名行。

translations.literal: He was addicted to wine and sex and did not pursue name and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned in wine and women and cared nothing for reputation.

sentences.zh: 契弟暉，歷涇州長史、新平太守，有惠政。

translations.literal: Qi's younger brother Hui served as Chief Clerk of Jingzhou and Administrator of Xinping and had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's brother Hui was Jingzhou chief clerk and Xinping administrator with humane rule.

sentences.zh: 景明中，大使于忠賞粟二百石。

translations.literal: In Jingming the envoy Yu Zhong rewarded two hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming envoy Yu Zhong rewarded him two hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Youzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 孫善，儀同開府主簿。

translations.literal: His grandson Shan was Chief Clerk of the Equal-in-Office Opened Staff.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shan was chief clerk on an equal-to-three-excellencies staff.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：魏之諸將，罕立方面之功。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Among Wei's generals, few established merit on a regional scale.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes that few Wei generals won regional command.

sentences.zh: 尉元以寬雅之風，受將帥之任，取瑕丘如覆掌，克彭城猶拾遺，擒將馘醜，威名遠被。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan with his easy, elegant wind received the generals' commission; taking Xiaqiu was like turning the palm, taking Pengcheng like picking up what was lost; capturing generals and severing ugly heads, his martial name spread far.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan took Xiaqiu as easily as turning his hand and Pengcheng as lightly as picking up a dropped object, capturing enemy leaders until his fame spread far.

sentences.zh: 位極公老，聖主乞言。

translations.literal: His rank reached the highest duke and elder; the sage ruler begged his words.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the highest rank and the emperor sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 無乃近世之一人歟？

translations.literal: Is he not nearly a man of the recent age?
translations.idiomatic: Was he not among the finest men of recent times?

sentences.zh: 白曜有敦正之風，出當薄伐，席卷三齊，如風靡草，接物有禮，海垂欣慰。

translations.literal: Baiyao had a wind of honest uprightness; going out to undertake a light punitive campaign, he swept the Three Qi like wind laying low grass; in receiving people he had ritual, and the sea margin sighed in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao campaigned with upright severity, swept the Three Qi like wind through grass, treated people courteously, and won the coast's relief.

sentences.zh: 其勞固不細矣。

translations.literal: His labor was indeed not slight.
translations.idiomatic: His labor was no small thing.

sentences.zh: 功名難處，追猜嬰戮，宥賢議勤，未聞於斯日也。

translations.literal: Merit and name are hard to dwell in; pursued by suspicion he met slaughter—pardoning the worthy and debating merit was not heard of on that day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet merit invites suspicion; he was slaughtered while pardoning merit went unheard.

translations.literal: The Kaoyi says: "Probably 'again' should be 'zai,' a particle, not meaning to pass through cold and heat twice."
translations.idiomatic: Kaoyi: 'again' should read 'zai,' a particle, not 'twice through cold and heat.'

translations.idiomatic: On frostbitten knee walkers: Ji, Dian, and Ju editions read one character as wa; Baibaina, Nan, and Bei editions read another.

translations.literal: These two lines say that after Wei occupied Qing and Qi, Wei Yuan was Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The lines mean that after Wei took Qing and Qi, Wei Yuan held Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 「海岱」指今山東一帶，作「岱」是。

translations.literal: 'Hai Dai' refers to present-day Shandong; writing 'Dai' is correct.
translations.idiomatic: 'Hai Dai' means Shandong; 'Dai' is correct.

translations.literal: What foolish sincerity sees — in all editions the character 'foolish' is missing; now supplemented according to Cefu, juan 364
translations.idiomatic: On 'foolish sincerity': editions lack 'foolish'; restored from Cefu 364

translations.idiomatic: On 'later kings': editions miswrite hou as yin; corrected from Cefu 55

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes say: When filial piety and brotherliness reach their height they penetrate to the spirits and shine over the four seas — these three lines are from the Xiaojing Ganying chapter; probably the character 'Odes' is wrong, or under 'the Odes say' the original quoted the Odes and then the Xiaojing, and the transmitted text under 'say' has lost words.
translations.idiomatic: The 'Odes' citation is likely the Xiaojing; the text may have dropped words.

sentences.zh: 故尊公以三 北史卷二五尉元傳「公」作「老」。

translations.literal: Therefore honor the Duke with the Three — Beishi, juan 25, Wei Yuan biography writes 'elder' for 'Duke.'
translations.idiomatic: Beishi 25 reads 'elder' for 'Duke' in 'honor the Three.'

sentences.zh: 按這裏是說「三老五更」，下云：「事更以五」，則上自應作「尊老以三」。

translations.literal: Here it speaks of the Three Elders and Five Worthies; below it says 'serve the Worthies with five,' so above it should read 'honor the elders with three.'
translations.idiomatic: The passage concerns Three Elders and Five Worthies; 'Duke' is likely wrong for 'elders.'

sentences.zh: 「公」字當誤。

translations.literal: The character 'Duke' must be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: 'Duke' is erroneous.

sentences.zh: 抽怛於懷 李慈銘云：「『抽』當作『妯』，用詩『憂心且妯』也。

translations.literal: Chou dan in the breast — Li Ciming says: "'Chou' should be 'zhou,' using the Odes 'anxious heart yet zhou'; the original character is 'you.'"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming: 'chou' should be 'zhou' from the Odes, original you.

sentences.zh: 本字作『怞』。」

translations.literal: The vulgar form is written 'you.'"
translations.idiomatic: Vulgar form: you."

sentences.zh: 及士治伐吳 諸本「治」作「冶」。

translations.literal: And when Shi Zhi campaigned against Wu — in all editions 'Zhi' is written as 'Ye.'
translations.idiomatic: On Wang Jun's Wu campaign: editions write Ye for Zhi.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘云：「『冶』當作『治』，王濬字士治。

translations.literal: Li Ciming says: "'Ye' should be 'Zhi'; Wang Jun's style name is Shi Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming: Ye should be Zhi; Wang Jun's style was Shi Zhi.

sentences.zh: 」按李說是，「冶」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: According to Li's statement it is so; the character 'Ye' is erroneous—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Li is correct; Ye is a corruption, now corrected.

sentences.zh: 位登帝伯 冊府卷八七五

translations.literal: Rank reaching imperial peer — Cefu, juan 875
translations.idiomatic: Rank reaching imperial peer — Cefu, scroll 875

sentences.zh: 〈一０三七二頁〉
「帝」作「嘗」，即「常」，明本避諱改。

translations.literal: "Imperial" is written as "once," that is "chang"; the Ming edition changed it to avoid taboo.
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial" reads "once" (chang); the Ming edition altered it to avoid taboo.

sentences.zh: 按「帝伯」罕見。

translations.literal: Note: "imperial peer" is rare.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "imperial peer" is uncommon.

sentences.zh: 嚴可均全後魏文卷三四錄此文，也作「常」，當是以意改。

translations.literal: Yan Kejun's Complete Northern Wei Writings, juan 34, also records this text as "chang," probably altered by intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Kejun's collected Northern Wei texts also read chang, likely an intentional change.

sentences.zh: 「常伯」一般指侍中，初學記卷一二侍中條、御覽卷二一九侍中下引漢書典職、環濟要略，通典卷二一侍中條引干寶注漢官，都以為見於尚書立政篇的常伯相當於漢以後的侍中。

translations.literal: "Changbo" generally means Palace Attendant; Chuxueji juan 12 Palace Attendant section, Taiping Yulan juan 219 Palace Attendant lower citing Hanshu Dianzhi and Huanji Yaolue, Tongdian juan 21 Palace Attendant citing Gan Bao's commentary on the Han Offices—all hold that the changbo seen in the Shangshu Lizheng chapter corresponds to the Palace Attendant after Han.
translations.idiomatic: "Changbo" usually means Palace Attendant; early texts equate the Shangshu's changbo with the Han and later Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 疑作「常伯」是，但此傳不言白曜曾為侍中，今不改。

translations.literal: Probably writing "changbo" is correct, but this biography does not say Baiyao ever was Palace Attendant—now not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Changbo may be correct, but the biography never says Baiyao was Palace Attendant; left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 和第二子僧濟 北、殿、局三本「和」作「契」，百衲、南、汲三本作「和」。

translations.literal: He and Qi's second son Sengji — Bei, Dian, and Ju editions write "He" as "Qi"; Baibaina, Nan, and Ji editions write "He."
translations.idiomatic: On "He and Qi's second son Sengji": Bei, Dian, and Ju read He as Qi; Baibaina, Nan, and Ji read He.

sentences.zh: 按上不出「和」名，不知「和」是誰，似作「契」是。

translations.literal: According to the text above, the name "He" is not given; one does not know who "He" is—it seems writing "Qi" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The text above never names He; Qi seems correct.

sentences.zh: 但若是契次子，按傳例應云：「昇

translations.literal: But if he were Qi's second son, by the biography's pattern it should read: "Sheng
translations.idiomatic: If he were Qi's second son, the biography should read "Sheng

translations.literal: 〈or Sengdu〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈or Sengdu〉

sentences.zh: 弟僧濟。

translations.literal: younger brother Sengji."
translations.idiomatic: younger brother Sengji."

sentences.zh: 」或上有脫文。

translations.literal: Or there are missing words above.
translations.idiomatic: Or words are missing above.

sentences.zh: 北本以下當是以意改，今從百衲本。

translations.literal: The Bei edition and below probably altered by intent; now follow the Baibaina edition.
translations.idiomatic: Later editions likely changed the text deliberately; the Baibaina reading is followed.
